crop.notes: Whole 'Answers to Correspondents' column; only the answer to 'Sport' concerns Allen.

ocr.notes: Accurate apart from the first lines ('P pee ROC eee' for 'Subscriber.—Heenan and Sayers fought in 1860') and 'Oambridge' for 'Cambridge'.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch answered a reader that Tom Allen was never prize-ring champion of England, but won the silver cup for the championship at boxing in England from Charles Davis at Cambridge in 1878.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Thursday, March 15, 1888, page 4.

facts.fact: Allen won the silver cup for the championship at boxing in England against Charles Davis at Cambridge in 1878, and still held the cup in 1888
The Post-Dispatch stated that Allen was never champion of the prize ring in England
Allen won the championship of America from Mike McCoole

notes: The paper's claim that Allen was never English prize-ring champion conflicts with the existing fact that he claimed the English title on arriving in America.
